title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Passes 4,000 Deaths
summary:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo, a country in central Africa, is fighting a very large outbreak of Ebola. Ebola is a dangerous disease caused by a virus. Officials announced the outbreak on May 15. Now the health ministry says more than 4,000 people have died. Its latest figures show 4,018 deaths among about 8,300 confirmed cases, which is nearly half of the cases. The outbreak is caused by a rare virus called Bundibugyo, and there is no known treatment or vaccine for it.

Fighting the outbreak is hard. Some health workers gathered in the city of Bunia and asked to be paid wages they are owed. Officials quickly sent them away. Some of them do surveillance work, which means finding people who were near a sick patient. Front-line workers have also gone on strike several times, and that slows the work.

Safety is another problem. A senior United Nations official said soldiers burned a camp that included a transit center for Ebola patients while they were searching for weapons. About 19,000 people who were living in the camp had to leave. The official said that when a center is lost, the money and staff that built it are lost too, and the work has to start again.

There is also some news that is more hopeful. Confirmed cases have slowed, from about 850 a week in mid-July to an average of 490 a week in September. But Africa CDC says that could be partly because of insecurity and trouble getting communities to cooperate. In some places the spread has slowed down, and in others it has sped up.
why_it_matters: A large outbreak with no known treatment shows how important it is to pay health workers, keep treatment centers safe and help communities work with doctors.
